note: Lens items about AlexNet, the transformer, and era-by-era belief and dissent are outside this brief: a one-minute Mark I short limited to four claims with no quotes. They are not scored against the film. They appear once as a global minor note.

issues.problem: The picture correctly turns only the dials fed by lit cells. The narration says 'nudge each dial', which teaches the wrong rule: a 15-year-old learns that every weight moves, and an expert notices the mismatch with the picture.
issues.fix: Rewrite as 'When it guesses wrong, the motors nudge the dials of the lit cells a little toward the right answer.' This stays inside the mk1-rule claim. Keep the 'nudge' beat anchored to the word 'nudge'.

issues.problem: The film never explains how the machine forms a guess (lit cells send signals through dials and the needle follows the total). Without that, 'nudge toward the right answer' is magic and depth stops at 'it tries again'. The runtime is 44.75 s against a 60 s target, so there is room.
issues.fix: Add a claim to claims.json for the weighted sum against a threshold (source: Wikipedia, Perceptron). Then expand or follow L0105 with a line such as 'Each lit cell pushes on the needle through its dial; the needle follows the sum.' In ch01-s03, pulse the threads into the response unit on that line before the needle snaps.

issues.problem: The push-in to K2 starts around 'then' (about 39.2 s) and crops the retina out of frame. At the climax ('right', 42.7 s) the viewer sees the needle and the lantern but not the shape it got right. The payoff depends on a small italic caption.
issues.fix: Keep the retina in frame through 'right'. Either frame K2 so it holds the retina bar and the response unit (drop the dial rack's left half instead), or add a small lit inset of the presented bar beside the gauge from 'suddenly' onwards.

issues.problem: Four wrong answers followed by one right one reads as luck rather than learning. 'Learned to see' needs the machine to get both shapes right.
issues.fix: If the real PERCEPTRON_RUN record supports it, add presentation 6 (vertical bar, answer VERTICAL, right) in a 2–3 s tail after 'right'. The lantern should flare again and the caption should read 'presentation 6 · said "vertical" — right'. If the record does not support it, do not fake it: hold on p5 and let the caption say so.

issues.problem: Threads run from the 400-cell retina into an unexplained 8×8 board of 64 dials. A young viewer will assume one dial per cell and be confused by the count. The real machine had a randomly wired association layer in between.
issues.fix: Change the rack header to 'ASSOCIATION UNITS · WEIGHTS', or add a sub-caption 'each dial weighs a random handful of cells'. This needs a one-line claim for the random retina-to-A-unit wiring.

issues.problem: At the wide framing during 'nudge each dial a little', the turning dial pointers are tiny ticks. The central mechanism of the film is hard to read on a phone-sized screen.
issues.fix: Make the pointers and arc arrows on the moving dials 1.5–2× thicker for p1's turn, or push in briefly on the rack across 'nudge … dial' (about +6.2 to +7.5 s) before returning wide.

issues.problem: Two problems. 'Called it a perceptron' is not in claims.json, which breaks the brief's only-these-claims guardrail. 'The psychologist who built it' overstates mk1-builder, which credits 'Rosenblatt's project'. The new term also never appears on screen.
issues.fix: Add a claim that Rosenblatt named the perceptron (1957–58) and soften the line to 'The psychologist whose project built it, Frank Rosenblatt, called it a perceptron.' In ch01-s02, letter 'PERCEPTRON' beneath the name card on the word 'perceptron' (18.2 s into the shot).

issues.problem: The film ends 2.1 s after 'right' and the D-major bloom barely has room to land. With nothing after it, the payoff feels clipped and the runtime is 75% of target.
issues.fix: Extend ch01-s03 by about 3 s, which also fits the p6 confirmation, and hold on the lit lantern. Have m01 ring out over the hold and fade to black on a held chord.

issues.problem: Lens note: there is no sense of what came next: what people believed about the perceptron, who dissented (Minsky and Papert, 1969), or how long the doubt lasted. Under this brief that is out of scope, but it is also why curiosity tops out.
issues.fix: Only if the brief is widened: add one researched claim and a closing line ('Its critics would soon call it a dead end. They were early.') over the held lantern. Otherwise leave it.

issues.problem: Automated QA flags a loud clip head on L0101 (-29 dBFS), and the narration stem sits at -22.4 LUFS against a -18 target with 4 dB of limiting. The opening word may sound clipped.
issues.fix: Re-trim L0101 with a 30 ms pre-roll and fade-in, re-level the stem to -18 LUFS before the mix, then re-run film-assemble.

best_moments: ch01-s02 (6.0–12.0 s): the '400 light cells' annotation lands on 'four', and one row and then one column flare under brackets on 'twenty by twenty'. The number is taught by the picture.
ch01-s02 (17.5–18.5 s): a scattered handful of potentiometers visibly turn and glint exactly on 'motors could turn'. This sets up the learning shot.
ch01-s02 (21.5–24 s): Rosenblatt straightens and presents the machine on his name, with a clean name card.

ch01-s03: a real perceptron-rule training record, not a fake animation. The needle snaps to the wrong answer on each 'wrong', only the fired dials turn on 'nudge', and the response lantern flares on 'right'.
m01: the score keeps its D-major arrival back until the exact word 'right' (bar 12 lands at 42.67 s). The film's emotional turn comes through the music.
